draft.title: Writing about country
card: Writing about country is a framework of ideas about place and belonging. It looks at the bonds between people and the places they know.
A place can be a farm, a suburb, a coastline or a childhood street. It can be real or remembered, and it can be loved, lost or left behind.
Strong writing in this framework shows how a place shapes a person's memories, identity or sense of home. Specific details, such as the smell of rain on dry ground, make the bond feel real.
For many First Nations peoples, Country means land, waters and sky as a living part of identity, culture and kinship. Writers who use this idea should treat it with care and respect.
draft.remember: Writing about country explores how people and places shape each other.

a.q: Which idea is at the centre of the framework of writing about country?
opts: The bond between people and the places they know
The reasons people speak out against a rule
The way games and sport show human character
The way a person changes over a long journey
a.why: This framework is about place and belonging, and how people connect to where they live or have lived. The other options describe the frameworks of protest, play and personal journeys.

b.q: Mia writes about her grandfather's wheat farm near Horsham, which was sold last year. She describes the dusty gate and the sound of the wind in the silos. Which part of the framework does her piece mainly explore?
opts: How a loved place holds memory and a sense of home
How a group resists a decision made by authority
How a person grows by travelling somewhere new
How imagination turns an ordinary space into a game
b.why: Mia's piece is built around a particular place she knew and has lost, and the details show what it meant to her. It does not centre on resistance, travel or play, which belong to other frameworks.
b.clue: Focus on what the farm means to Mia.

a.best: The bond between people and the places they know

b.best: How a loved place holds memory and a sense of home

a.q: A student is planning a piece for the framework of writing about country. Which plan fits it best?
opts: A woman recalls the river town where she grew up
A student organises a walkout over a new school rule
Two brothers invent a game that lasts all summer
A teenager gains confidence after starting a new job
a.why: Recalling the town where she grew up centres on her bond with a place she knows and what it means to her. The walkout, the game and the new job focus on resistance, play and personal growth, which belong to other frameworks.
a.clue: Which plan centres on a bond with somewhere known?
